sentences.text: Scientists identify this ancient duck by unique features on its humerus bone, the upper arm bone that connects to the wing.
Mionetta is one of the earliest and best-known fossil ducks, with the type species M. blanchardi represented by thousands of specimens.
The genus Mionetta was described by Livezey and Martin in 1988.
Many species originally assigned to Mionetta were previously classified within the genus Anas.
Mionetta belongs to the family Anatidae.
The Paleobi Database lists Oxyurinae as the parent group for Mionetta.
Mionetta lived between 33.9 and 15.98 million years ago, from the Rupelian to the Burdigalian stages.
It inhabited Western and Central Europe, including France, Germany, and the Czech Republic, and possibly Kazakhstan.

There is a debate regarding Mionetta's classification: a 2008 study placed it in the subfamily Oxyurinae, while a 2022 study positioned it basally in Anatidae outside the split between Oxyurinae, Anatinae, and Anserinae.
